title: Peri-Ictal and Para-Ictal Psychiatric Symptoms in Patients with Epilepsy: Frequent but Underrecognized Phenomena
content: Psychiatric manifestations that occur in temporal proximity to seizures contribute substantially to morbidity in people with epilepsy (PWE) but are often overlooked. These symptoms are usually transient and do not fit conventional psychiatric diagnostic timelines. This narrative review synthesizes the phenomenology, frequency, risk factors, and proposed mechanisms of peri-ictal (pre-ictal, ictal, and post-ictal) and para-ictal phenomena, drawing on searches of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus through 21 August 2026. Pre-ictal symptoms most often comprise dysphoria, anxiety and other mood changes emerging hours to days before seizures. Ictal psychiatric symptoms are brief and stereotyped; ictal fear is the best-characterized example and is frequently associated with mesial temporal networks, whereas ecstatic auras have been linked to the dorsal anterior insula. Post-ictal manifestations include anxiety, depressive symptoms, psychosis, and manic or hypomanic states, although prevalence estimates vary substantially across settings and definitions. Para-ictal psychosis may occur during improved seizure control, as described in forced normalization and alternative psychosis. The available evidence is limited by heterogeneous definitions, small tertiary-center cohorts, and case-based literature. Recognition requires a careful chronology of symptoms in relation to seizures, collateral history, and attention to recent therapeutic changes. Prospective multicenter studies and validated peri-ictal assessment tools are needed.
